# Northvale Analysis Meeting 2026-05-20

Storage-time review. Present: [[maja-kovac]], Ines, [[elias-moreau]], [[mei-lin-zhou]] (first half), [[paolo-ferrante]] (for freezer history).

## Discussion

Elias and Maja presented the [[northvale-storage-time-qc-report]]. Matching on draw date has balanced storage within sets, cfDNA yield barely moves with storage, and genomic DNA contamination is equally common in cases and controls. Paolo explained the two freezer moves (2011 and 2018) and that the 2011 move included a 6-hour power cut with temperature logged at -62 at worst.

Maja raised the remaining problem: across matched sets, storage time and time to diagnosis are correlated, because long time-to-diagnosis cases come from early recruitment. If old samples lose signal, the null result beyond five years could partly be a storage effect. [[patel-2026-prediagnostic-methylation-cps3]] was mentioned as a comparison with shorter storage and a similar fall-off.

## Decisions

- Add a model with storage time interacting with the score, and a sensitivity analysis restricted to samples without freezer moves.
- Paolo compiles the full freezer history for 2004 to 2012.
- The question stays open ([[does-storage-time-confound-the-northvale-methylation-signal]]).
